answer: Initially, the Go CLI was the implementation behind Phase 0 proxy commands and the authoritative behavioral specification for the TypeScript port. Once most commands had been ported, that blanket authority was narrowed: Go needed to be consulted for remaining wrapped commands and changes affecting established parity behavior, while other TypeScript work followed normal engineering standards. Later, after the remaining Go delegations were removed and no TypeScript command spawned `supabase-go`, the Go code was deleted because it no longer served the CLI.
evidence: `src/legacy/` started as a from-scratch, strict 1:1 port of the Go CLI (`apps/cli-go/`): every command began as a Phase 0 proxy to the Go binary, then moved to a native TypeScript implementation (Phase 1+).

While that was true, treating `apps/cli-go/` as the unconditional authority for anything touching `src/legacy/` was correct — nearly every change was either wrapping a new command or replacing its proxy, and the Go source was the only available spec for what the command should do.
Per `apps/cli/docs/go-cli-porting-status.md` (removed, CLI-2432), 95 of 103 legacy leaf commands (~92%) are natively ported; only 8 remain Phase 0 proxies.

ADR 0016 says `apps/cli-go/` must be consulted when maintaining or replacing one of the remaining wrapped commands, or when a change to an already-ported command touches its established parity surface: command and flag names, stdout and stderr text, exit codes, documented side effects, or telemetry semantics.

No command in the TypeScript CLI spawns `supabase-go` anymore. That leaves `apps/cli-go/` — roughly 300 tracked files across three Go modules (the root CLI module, the `fsevents` helper module, and the separately-tagged `pkg` module) — serving nothing.
Delete `apps/cli-go/` entirely. The CLI ships as a single compiled binary per platform (`packages/cli-<platform>/bin/supabase`), built by `apps/cli/scripts/build.ts` with no Go compilation step.

answer: Phel implements persistent collections in PHP under `src/php/Lang/Collections/`, and Phel literals compile to them. Vectors use a 32-way trie; maps use a small `PersistentArrayMap` that promotes to a HAMT-based `PersistentHashMap`; lists are singly linked; sets use the hash map; lazy sequences cache realized elements; and structs are fixed-key map subclasses. Queues, sorted maps, and sorted sets follow the same persistent-collection rules.
evidence: `src/php/Lang/Collections/` implements persistent structures in PHP, and they are what Phel literals compile to.

| Vector | `PersistentVector`, 32-way trie |
| Map | `PersistentArrayMap` (small), promoted to `PersistentHashMap` (HAMT) |
| List | `PersistentList`, singly linked |
| Set | `PersistentHashSet`, over the hash map |
| Lazy seq | `LazySeq`, realised and cached per element |
| Struct | `AbstractPersistentStruct`, fixed-key map subclassed by `defstruct` |
`Queue/`, `SortedMap/`, `SortedSet/` follow the same rules; the table lists what a compiled literal produces.
